candidates.change_summary: Delete the require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0) statement so callers can overwrite their existing guess.
Delete the require(msg.value == 1 ether) statement so lockInGuess succeeds with any msg.value.
Delete the assignment of the guess hash so guesses[msg.sender].guess stays bytes32(0).
Replace the stored target block with block.number so settle's blockhash is taken for the lock-in block itself.
Delete the assignment of the target block so guesses[msg.sender].block remains 0 and settle always reverts.
Delete the guard `require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0);` so settle() no longer reverts for accounts with no locked-in guess.
Delete the guard `require(block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block);` so settle() can be called before the target block, using blockhash(0) semantics.
Replace `blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block)` with `blockhash(block.number)` so the answer is computed from the current block instead of the guessed block.
Move `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0;` to before the answer computation so blockhash(0) is used, changing the answer and thus whether the payout branch triggers.

Delete the reset statement `guesses[msg.sender].block = 0;` so after settling, repeated calls to settle() revert differently than in the original (where the second call reverts on block != 0 versus first call succeeding).
